Definition: apparently a primary verb; to creak (squeak), i.e. (by analogy) to grate the teeth (in frenzy):--gnash.
BiblicalUsage: Wherever the demon takes the boy it tears him, and he foams and gnashes with his teeth and pines away. Wherever it takes him it tears him, and he foams and gnashes with his teeth and pines away, and the disciples could not cast it out.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the gnashing is the sound of the affliction itself: the boy's body is the battleground, and only Jesus ends it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
